title: Canonical Signed Profile Registry, Consumer Notification & Rollback Flow
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Teams rely on Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) when pinning models and choosing routing policies. Today profiles are published as files with ad-hoc metadata and no canonical identity, which makes consumers fragile to silent changes, complicates audits, and prevents automated rollbacks.
goal: Ship a canonical, cryptographically signed performance profile registry with immutable versioned records, consumer subscription/notification hooks, and automated rollback semantics to reduce regression incidents and enable safe model profile updates.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical registry endpoint exists (GET/POST) that returns a signed JSON profile manifest with a unique profile_id and semantic version
Publishing flow requires an automated verification run (benchmarks pass) and signs the profile with the platform signing key
Consumers can opt-in to webhook or event-stream notifications for profile changes and receive semantic diffs
A rollback API exists to pin consumers to previous profile versions (immutable history) with authorization checks
Audit log entries created for publish/rollback with signer, checksum, and benchmark run id
E2E test that simulates a profile regression and demonstrates notification + automated fallback within SLO
plan: Design registry schema and signing format (include checksum, model_version, perf_stats, benchmark_suite_id)
Implement publishing pipeline that runs verified-benchmark CI and produces signed manifests
Build registry service with read/query endpoints and write endpoints gated by CI and RBAC
Add consumer subscription API (webhook + event stream) and a delta/diff payload format
Expose rollback/pin API for consumers and console UI to view profile history
Coordinate with SDK teams to add transparent profile fetch + verify in client libraries
Document operational runbooks and KMS key rotation policy for signing key
stakeholders: Engineering: Liam Chen (owner), Priya Nair (runtime), Mateo Alvarez (benchmarks)
risks: Signing key compromise or rotation complexity could break consumers if clients don't verify signatures
Benchmarks flakiness may block legitimate profile updates; need stable CI and retry semantics
Performance of registry reads at scale if SDKs fetch on hot paths; need caching and CDN
Migration risk for existing profiles and pinning semantics for Dedicated/Private deployments
rollout_plan: MVP: registry read-only + signed historical export (runtime-1.20 alpha) exposed to internal teams
Phase 1: publishing pipeline + verified benchmarking gating, internal canaries with core clients
Phase 2: public consumer subscription API, SDK verify helpers, and console UI for profile history
Phase 3: automated rollback policies (policy engine) and Partner Docs for Dedicated/Private customers
Gradual rollout with feature flag and telemetry to track read rates and failure modes
metrics: Number of consumers subscribed to profile updates
Mean time to detect and rollback a profile-caused regression
Fraction of clients verifying signature of fetched profile
Incidents attributable to profile changes (goal: 0 for public profiles)
implementation_notes: Use platform KMS for signing; prefer asymmetric signing (RS256) with certificate rotation metadata
Registry storage implemented as append-only ledger table with immutable rows and sequence numbers
Expose both compact and human-readable profile encodings; SDKs should verify signature and checksum
Bench harness must produce deterministic artifacts (seeded runs) and publish run ids linked in manifest
Cache control headers and CDN recommended for read endpoints; limit frequent fetches via TTL
consumer_requirements: Clients must fetch profile and validate signature before using pinning/routing decisions
Provide opt-in webhook or event-stream subscription; on receive clients should fetch latest manifest and validate
Clients that opt-in to auto-rollback must expose a safe fallback threshold and alerting mechanism
